                                                           Abstract
     Second-order optimization methods are computationally expensive for large-scale problems. Re-
     cently, Doikov, Chayti, and Jaggi (ICML 2023) proposed the LazyCRN method that reduces com-
     putation by studying the gradient complexity of second-order methods. Their method can achieve
     a gradient complexity of O(d¯ + d¯1/2 ϵ−3/2 ) and O(d¯ + d¯1/2 ϵ−1/2 ) for nonconvex and convex
     optimization, respectively, where d¯ is the effective dimension and ϵ is the target precision. Very
     recently, Adil, Bullins, Sidford, and Zhang (NeurIPS 2025) improved the gradient complexity to
     O(d¯ + d¯1/3 ϵ−3/2 ln18 ϵ−1 ) for nonconvex optimization. However, the tightness of these methods
     remains open. In this work, we propose new methods that achieve an improved complexity of
     O(d¯ + d¯1/3 ϵ−3/2 ) and O((d¯ + d¯13/21 ϵ−2/7 ) ln d)

     tively, improving best-known results for both setups.

1. Introduction
Minimizing differentiable functions has wide applications in machine learning, including matrix
completion (Hardt, 2014), phase retrieval (Candes et al., 2015), and neural network training (Le-
Cun et al., 2015). In this work, we focus on second-order methods (Nesterov, 2018, Chapter 4),
which achieve faster convergence rates compared to their first-order counterparts. Over the past two
decades, optimal second-order methods measured by oracle complexities (Nemirovskij and Yudin,
1983) (i.e., the number of gradient and Hessian calls) have been proposed. Remarkably, for non-
convex problems, Nesterov and Polyak (2006) proposed the optimal second-order method known
as cubic regularized Newton (CRN). For convex problems, Monteiro and Svaiter (2013) proposed a
near-optimal method known as accelerated Newton proximal extragradient (A-NPE), and recently
Carmon et al. (2022a); Kovalev and Gasnikov (2022) proposed optimal A-NPE methods.
    However, oracle-optimal methods could be slow in practice due to the computational burden
of solving auxiliary problems. An example is cutting-plane methods: while they have long been

require solving non-trivial subproblems, and thus a wealth of research has been dedicated to making

methods could also be costly due to the computation of the Hessian oracle and matrix inversion. It
motivates us to better model computation for designing faster second-order methods.
    Recently, Doikov et al. (2023) proposed to measure the complexity of second-order methods by
equivalent gradient calls. This new computation model takes into account that Hessian oracles are
usually more expensive than gradient oracles in practice, and thus treats a single Hessian query as
equivalent to d¯ gradient queries, where d¯ is the effective dimension. Additionally, for second-order
methods, the equivalent gradient complexity can be easily translated into actual computational com-
plexity (see Section 3.2). Subsequently, new second-order methods with low equivalent gradient
complexities are proposed (Doikov et al., 2023; Chayti et al., 2024; Adil et al., 2025).
    For nonconvex problems, Doikov et al. (2023) proposed the lazy cubic regularized Newton
(LazyCRN) method and showed that it can find an ϵ-stationary point a nonconvex function in an
equivalent gradient complexity of O(d¯ + d¯1/2 ϵ−3/2 ), which improves over the O(dϵ     ¯ −3/2 ) com-
plexity by original CRN method (Nesterov and Polyak, 2006). Very recently, Adil et al. (2025)
proposed a novel restarted approximate Hessian accelerated gradient descent (RAH-AGD) method,
achieving an improved complexity of O(d¯+ d¯1/3 ϵ−3/2 ln18 ϵ−1 ) by applying the restarted AGD (Li
and Lin, 2023) preconditioned with a carefully designed approximate lazy Hessian. However, the
ϵ-dependency in the complexity bound of RAH-AGD involves an extra ln18 ϵ−1 factor compared to
the Ω(ϵ−3/2 ) lower bound (Carmon et al., 2020a), suggesting room for improvement.
    For convex problems, Chayti et al. (2024) showed that LazyCRN can find an ϵ-global solution
in the complexity of O(d¯ + d¯1/2 ϵ−1/2 ), which also improves the O(dϵ  ¯ −1/2 ) complexity by CRN
(Nesterov and Polyak, 2006). However, the dependency in ϵ is far from the optimal Ω(ϵ−2/7 ) lower
bound (Arjevani et al., 2019). The acceleration of LazyCRN for convex problems has been regarded
as an open problem in in the prior literature (Doikov et al., 2023; Doikov and Grapiglia, 2025).

Our Contributions. Inspired by known results, we improve gradient complexities for both convex
and nonconvex problems by proposing new second-order methods:

   1. For nonconvex problems, we propose a novel second-order method called Nonconvex Accel-

2. Related Works
In the following, we review additional related works on convex and nonconvex optimization.

2.1. Convex optimization
For first-order methods, Nesterov (1983) proposed the accelerated gradient descent (AGD) that can
find an ϵ-solution to a convex problem with O(ϵ−1/2 ) gradient calls, which is oracle-optimal as it
matches the Ω(ϵ−1/2 ) lower bound (Nemirovskij and Yudin, 1983). In low dimensions, the cutting
plane methods (CPM) typically enjoy better theoretical upper bounds and also achieve the optimal
gradient complexity of O(d ln ϵ−1 ) (Nemirovskij and Yudin, 1983; Braverman et al., 2020). A
variety of works such as (Vaidya, 1989, 1996; Lee et al., 2015; Jiang et al., 2020) further improved
the computational costs in auxiliary problems in CPMs.
    For second-order methods, Nesterov and Polyak (2006) proposed the cubic regularized Newton
(CRN) method that requires a O(dϵ   ¯ −1/2 ) equivalent gradient complexity. Furthermore, Nesterov
(2008) proposed the accelerated cubic regularized Newton (A-CRN) method that achieves a better
complexity of O(dϵ ¯ −1/3 ). Later, Monteiro and Svaiter (2013) proposed the accelerated Newton
proximal extragradient (A-NPE) method that further improves the complexity to O(dϵ    ¯ −2/7 ln ϵ−1 ),
which is refined to O(dϵ ¯ −2/7 ) independently by Carmon et al. (2022a); Kovalev and Gasnikov
(2022), whose ϵ dependencies are optimal as they match the lower bound provided by Arjevani et al.
(2019). Additionally, Jiang and Mokhtari (2023) proposed the accelerated quasi-Newton     proximal
extragradient (A-QNPE) method with a gradient complexity of O d1/5 ϵ−2/5 ln(dϵ−2 ) .

Definition 3.1 We call x̂ ∈ Rd an ϵ-(global) solution to Problem (1) if f (x̂) − f ∗ ≤ ϵ.

Definition 3.2 We call x̂ ∈ Rd an ϵ-stationary point to Problem (1) if ∥∇f (x̂)∥ ≤ ϵ.

5. Results for Convex Optimization

Building upon the NALEN algorithm for nonconvex problems, we further propose a double-loop
method CALEN for convex problems. In the outer loop (Algorithm 2), our algorithm applies the
Monteiro-Svaiter acceleration (Monteiro and Svaiter, 2013) that requires an MS oracle (formally
